key_insight: This paper evaluates how tabular foundation models behave when the data changes at test time, rather than only when training and testing data come from the same distribution. The core takeaway is that strong in-distribution performance does not necessarily guarantee robustness under real-world distribution shifts.
problem_solved: It addresses the gap in understanding whether tabular foundation models remain reliable when faced with out-of-distribution data, a common challenge in practical ML deployments.
method: Conducts an empirical evaluation of tabular foundation models under distribution shifts.
Compares model performance across shifted and non-shifted tabular settings to assess robustness.
Benchmarks TFMs against common baselines, including ensemble tree-based approaches, to contextualize results.
impact: For practitioners, this helps reveal when TFMs are suitable for deployment and when they may fail under changing data conditions. It supports better model selection, risk assessment, and robustness-aware evaluation for tabular ML applications.
visual_elements: A side-by-side diagram showing in-distribution vs out-of-distribution tabular data.
A performance bar chart comparing TFMs with tree-based baselines under different shift types.
An icon-based pipeline illustrating train → distribution shift → test outcome.
A radar/spider chart summarizing robustness across multiple shift scenarios.
paper_title: Empirical Evaluation of Out-Of-Distribution Performance of Tabular Foundation Models
paper_authors: Malena Loza, David Chushig-Muzo, Eva Milara, Luis Bote-Curiel, Luis Estrada-Petrocelli
